newsitem.title: USA: National Semi reports sharp rise in bookings.
newsitem.headline: National Semi reports sharp rise in bookings.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp Thursday said worldwide bookings were up more than 40 percent in the third quarter compared with last year's third quarter.

In a statement accompanying National Semiconductor's financial results for the three months ended in February, the company said its book-to-bill ratio remained above 1 in the quarter, although orders for the quarter were seasonally lower than the immediately preceding second quarter.

The Santa Clara, Calif-based company reported a profit of $42.8 million or $0.30 a share for the third quarter of fiscal 1997, compared with net income of $23.0 million or $0.17 a share for the comparable quarter of fiscal 1996.

"Our strong revenue and earnings performance for the quarter is one of the early paybacks of our new focus on operational excellence," said Brian Halla, president and chief executive officer. "Combined with the continuing recovery of our targeted market areas in analog, Ethernet, wireless and high-end personal computers, this improvement is reflected in our increased bottom line profitability."
According to First Call, analysts had expected the company to report a profit in the third quarter of $0.23 a share.

Sales for the third quarter, ended February 23, were $680.5 million, compared with sales of $600.3 million for the comparable quarter last year and $661.5 million in the second quarter of firscal 1997.
National Semiconductor said its gross margin recovered to 37.5 percent in the third quarter from 34.9 percent in the second quarter, and 38.6 percent in the third quarter a year ago.

For National's continuing businesses, that exclude Fairchild, the equivalent gross margin was 41.2 percent, compared with 38.3 percent for the second quarter and 42.3 percent for the third quarter a year ago.

National Semiconductor said personal computer orders led the company in year over year improvement and Local Area Network orders continued to be the company's largest single application area with meaningful growth over last year.
New product introductions in wireless products resulted in orders that doubled over last year. Bookings growth for analog and Fairchild products mirrored the company as a whole.
On a regional basis, bookings in Southeast Asia grew the most, but all regions were up over last year and showed less than traditional dips compared to second quarter levels, the company said.
